# dots command reference

On-demand reference, not required skill context. Prefer `dots COMMAND --help`; otherwise search for the command and read only its section. Do not load this file wholesale.

## dots

```text
Workflow tools for coding agents across local tools, services, and host integrations.
Use the available command groups for supported tasks; native tools remain available.
Help and skill generation work offline. Commands document their own effects and prerequisites.

Usage: dots [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  output     Publish and inspect immutable project evidence; publication does not accept tasks
  project    Initialize the workspace catalog and explicitly bind local Git projects
  github     Inspect GitHub CI evidence and PR review threads, and keep a PR watch list
  task       Track shared, claimable work for a project across concurrent sessions
  memory     Read and publish shared knowledge snapshots across machines
  substrate  Configure and inspect this machine's connection to the shared cross-machine remote
  sync       Keep this machine's substrate copy current with the shared remote
  skills     Export agent discovery documentation from this command tree

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## dots project share

```text
Without an action, report whether this checkout's project is registered, bound to a shared identity (which one), or declined on this machine, whether this machine shares (dots task share enable), and the shared identities known to knowledge. Names never establish identity: pick --bind with an identity that is this same repository, or --create for a new one. Each action registers the checkout first when needed. Binding replicates the project's goals and tasks while machine sharing is on, and its project knowledge; it queues existing trees at once. --decline remembers on this machine that the user does not want the project shared, so agents stop asking; binding later clears it.

Usage: dots project share [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --bind <SHARED_ID>
          Bind this checkout to an existing shared identity

      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --create <NAME>
          Create a shared identity with this display name and bind this checkout to it

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --decline
          Remember on this machine not to share this checkout's project

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots github ci

```text
Inspect CI for a PR, remote ref, commit, or exact workflow run/attempt.
Read-only; uses existing gh authentication.
With no subcommand, inspect the current branch's PR. Use --pr URL for another PR, --ref main or --sha SHA with --repo, or --run RUN_URL [--attempt N].
A ref selects its current commit, not the latest historical/scheduled run. Use gh run list for run discovery; pass a run URL here for diagnosis.
Details default to failed, cancelled, unknown and pending checks. --all includes passing/skipped checks; --name TEXT searches check names across all states. Both remain paged; summary always covers every check.
Failed or pending CI is data, not a command error. No checks does not mean CI passed.
Follow returned commands rather than constructing job references or selecting the latest run.

Usage: dots github ci [OPTIONS]
       dots github ci <COMMAND>

Commands:
  inspect  Inspect the selected CI target, with bounded evidence and complete scope counts
  logs     Read exact job logs from a URL, ID, or inspection reference
  output   Read GitHub-hosted check output; works for Actions and external-provider checks

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --ref <GIT_REF>
          Remote branch/tag, resolved once to a commit; use refs/heads/NAME to disambiguate

      --repo <[HOST/]OWNER/REPO>
          Explicit repository for numeric IDs or refs; URLs must agree with it

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --no-cache
          Bypass log caching and saved observations; fresh inspection always queries status

      --sha <SHA>
          Full commit SHA; inspects checks/statuses on that revision, not branch history

      --run <RUN>
          Workflow run URL or numeric ID; covers all event types without a PR

      --attempt <ATTEMPT>
          Exact run attempt; default resolves and pins the current attempt

      --pr <URL_OR_NUMBER>
          Explicit PR URL or number; URLs work outside a checkout

      --snapshot <REF>
          Read a saved observation (five-minute lifetime) without querying GitHub status

      --no-logs
          Skip automatic evidence retrieval (job logs and check output)

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum check details to show; summary always covers all checks

          [default: 20]

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Skip this many checks in failure-first order

          [default: 0]

      --all
          Include passed/skipped checks; still bounded by --limit and --offset

      --name <NAME>
          Case-insensitive literal substring in check names; includes all states

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots github ci logs

```text
Read exact job logs from a URL, ID, or inspection reference.
Copy REF from inspection output. PR updates and reruns do not redirect it. Job URLs and numeric IDs with --repo also work; no PR is required.
Use --search TEXT for a compact match index; follow Context for a compact window with up to three preceding lines.
For Go failures, follow Test output or use --test NAME to join RUN/NAME/CONT regions. Test output starts near a diagnostic when available; --start 1 reads from the beginning. Attribution is heuristic when concurrent packages interleave.
Use --start to page lines, resume a search, or continue attributed test output.
Search reports total and cursor-eligible matches, up to ten matching lines with context commands, and a command for the next ten matches. Follow saved-observation commands to search/page without GitHub queries. Saved job observations expire after five minutes; omit --snapshot to refresh. Downloads are cached for 24 hours, bounded at 512 MiB; excerpts are at most 16 KiB.
Missing logs include a gh fallback; do not infer a cause from status alone.
An aggregate job may only report a dependency failure: inspect the other failed jobs for the cause.

Usage: dots github ci logs [OPTIONS] <REFERENCE>

Arguments:
  <REFERENCE>
          Job URL, numeric ID with --repo, or reference returned by inspection

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --repo <[HOST/]OWNER/REPO>
          Explicit repository for numeric IDs or refs; URLs must agree with it

      --snapshot <SNAPSHOT>
          Reuse saved job metadata and logs without GitHub queries; omit to refresh

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --no-cache
          Bypass log caching and saved observations; fresh inspection always queries status

      --search <SEARCH>
          Find a literal, case-sensitive string; return a compact match index without context

      --test <TEST>
          Read output regions for an exact Go test name; preserves original line numbers

      --start <START>
          First line (one-based), or first eligible search match; default centers near a failure marker

      --lines <LINES>
          Maximum lines per window/test (default 100; search context 20)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots github ci output

```text
Read bounded GitHub check-run title, summary and text. Default windows use conservative compiler/failure markers; this is navigation, not a root-cause verdict. Use --start 1 for the beginning. Search context defaults to 20 lines with up to three preceding lines. Follow saved-observation commands to search/page without additional GitHub calls. Snapshots expire after five minutes; omit --snapshot to refresh. --annotations reads a fresh, bounded page of source diagnostics instead of text. Provider links and gh fallbacks remain available.

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

          Read the saved text observation without GitHub queries (five-minute lifetime)

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --no-cache
          Bypass log caching and saved observations; fresh inspection always queries status

      --start <START>
          First line (one-based), or first eligible search match

      --lines <LINES>
          Maximum lines per window (default 40; search context 20)

      --search <SEARCH>
          Literal, case-sensitive search; returns at most ten matches and context commands

      --annotations
          Read at most ten source annotations, with bounded messages

      --annotation-page <ANNOTATION_PAGE>
          Annotation page to read; follow the returned command to continue

          [default: 1]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots github reviews

```text
Read-only review-thread investigation. Defaults to unresolved threads, including outdated feedback. Opening-comment previews are not full conversations. Follow the returned thread command for replies and reviewed diff context. Use --json for agent workflows. General PR discussion, review submission, replies, resolution, and merging remain with gh or GitHub. Fresh lists traverse at most 1000 threads; conversations at most 200 comments. Query errors and incomplete traversals fail explicitly. Saved observations expire after five minutes; paging requires local credential/keychain access but makes no GitHub requests. Refresh preserves the filter and page size and restarts at offset zero. JSON has_more indicates continuation; complete means this page contains the entire matching collection.

Usage: dots github reviews [OPTIONS]
       dots github reviews <COMMAND>

Commands:
  thread  Read an exact review thread, its replies, and original reviewed diff context

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --pr <PR>
          PR URL or number; defaults to the current branch's PR

      --repo <[HOST/]OWNER/REPO>
          Explicit repository for numeric IDs or refs; URLs must agree with it

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --no-cache
          Bypass log caching and saved observations; fresh inspection always queries status

      --snapshot <SNAPSHOT>
          Page a saved thread index without GitHub queries

      --all
          Include resolved threads; outdated and resolved are separate states

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum thread previews to return

          [default: 10]

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Skip this many matching threads

          [default: 0]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots github reviews thread

```text
Read an exact review conversation. Diff context appears only at offset zero; later pages provide context_command to recover it. original_commit_id identifies the original reviewed revision; commit_id is GitHub's current comment association and may be a later commit. full_diff_hunk_command retrieves the untruncated review hunk, not surrounding file source. Use gh or the checkout for broader context. has_more indicates another page; complete means all comments are in this page. Snapshot reads need local credentials but make no GitHub requests.

Usage: dots github reviews thread [OPTIONS] <REFERENCE>

Arguments:
  <REFERENCE>
          Exact reference emitted by review-thread discovery

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --repo <[HOST/]OWNER/REPO>
          Explicit repository for numeric IDs or refs; URLs must agree with it

      --snapshot <SNAPSHOT>
          Page the saved conversation without GitHub queries

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum comments to return; each body is bounded to 4 KiB

          [default: 5]

      --no-cache
          Bypass log caching and saved observations; fresh inspection always queries status

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Skip this many comments in chronological API order

          [default: 0]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots github watch

```text
Agent-curated list of pull requests worth following, with cached status for pickers and agents. Add PRs you create or work on; adding records intent only and authorizes no CI fixes, monitoring, or merging. Entries are identified by canonical github.com PR URL.
No daemon: each row stores its next due check (60s before the first check or while CI is pending, 10 minutes once settled, 5 minutes after an error; merged or closed PRs are never checked again). Refresh fetches only due rows, one GraphQL request per 50 PRs, using existing gh authentication; concurrent refreshers never fetch the same PR twice. A failed check keeps the previous status and records the error. While a picker is open, its follow command refreshes due PRs; nothing runs otherwise.
The store is $XDG_STATE_HOME/dots/github/watch.sqlite3 (default ~/.local/state/dots/github/watch.sqlite3).

Usage: dots github watch [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  add      Add a PR, or update its checkout and sessions; idempotent, then refreshes that PR
  remove   Remove a PR from the list; an unlisted PR is not an error
  list     List watched PRs with cached status, newest first; no network
  show     Show one watched PR's cached status and description; no network
  follow   Refresh due PRs while a picker reads the output; prints a line when rows change
  refresh  Fetch status for PRs that are due; --all makes every open PR due first

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --repo <[HOST/]OWNER/REPO>
          Explicit repository for numeric IDs or refs; URLs must agree with it

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --no-cache
          Bypass log caching and saved observations; fresh inspection always queries status

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots github watch add

```text
Add a PR by URL, or update its entry: the original added time is kept, the checkout, agent session, and Rex session become the latest non-empty values, and the PR becomes due. The agent session is the invoking agent's: pi-$PI_SESSION_ID, claude-$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, or codex-$CODEX_SESSION_ID. The Rex session is the one the work belongs to: $REX_SESSION in a Rex terminal, otherwise $DOTS_REX_SESSION, which Pi workers inherit from the session that started them. Then refreshes this PR only; a GitHub failure is a warning in the result and never fails the add.

Usage: dots github watch add [OPTIONS] <URL>

Arguments:
  <URL>
          github.com pull request URL

Options:
      --checkout <PATH>
          Checkout the PR is worked from, stored as an absolute path; defaults to --directory or the current directory (a linked worktree itself, not its main checkout)

      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --repo <[HOST/]OWNER/REPO>
          Explicit repository for numeric IDs or refs; URLs must agree with it

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --no-cache
          Bypass log caching and saved observations; fresh inspection always queries status

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots github watch follow

```text
Meant as a picker's watch command. Prints `ready` at once, then refreshes PRs as they become due, exactly like refresh, and prints `changed` whenever the watched rows differ from what it last saw: a status change, a recorded error, or an entry another session added or removed. It has no effect beyond refreshing due PRs. Sleeps until the earliest due PR (between 1 and 60 seconds, re-checking at least every minute for new entries). Runs only while its reader is alive: it exits 0 when its output is closed or on SIGTERM, SIGINT, or SIGHUP. GitHub failures are recorded on their PRs and never end it; a storage failure does.

Usage: dots github watch follow [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --repo <[HOST/]OWNER/REPO>
          Explicit repository for numeric IDs or refs; URLs must agree with it

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --no-cache
          Bypass log caching and saved observations; fresh inspection always queries status

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots task

```text
Local work list shared by every session and worktree of one project: tasks, dependencies, claims, results, and issue/PR references. Git and GitHub remain the source of truth for code.
The project comes from the Git checkout at --directory, bound with dots project init; --project selects a registered project ID.
A claim marks the actor responsible for a task. It lasts until that actor releases, hands off, or closes it; Pi releases only an ending runtime's claims and preserves them on reload. Workers report results to their parent session, which records them.
A goal's tasks change only through its coordinator, the owner of its root claim (dots task goal coordinate); other sessions read them.
The catalog is $XDG_DATA_HOME/dots/workspace.sqlite3 (default ~/.local/share/dots/workspace.sqlite3).

Usage: dots task [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  goal          Create, list, and inspect goals: root tasks with a Markdown brief
  share         Replicate goals and task trees of bound projects across machines
  list          List unfinished root tasks; use --parent ID to drill down or --flat for every level
  ready         Unclaimed, unblocked open tasks without children
  show          Show one task with its result, evidence, and recent events
  result-event  Show an earlier result and its evidence
  events        Project history after an event seq, oldest first; use the last seen seq as a cursor
  event-kinds   List every kind an event can have
  add           Create an open task; --parent groups it under a larger task or goal
  claim         Claim a task, or the next ready one, for this session
  release       Release this session's claim on a task, or every claim it holds with --all
  update        Edit a task's fields, or replace its current result
  review        Record a result and move the task to review; clears the claim
  done          Close a task whose acceptance criteria are met
  hold          Pause a task with a reason and clear its claim; its descendants stay claimable
  drop          Close a task that will not be done; its dependents are unblocked
  reopen        Return a task to open; its result stays
  ref           Link issues, pull requests, and tickets to a task; nothing is sent to their provider
  dep           Manage prerequisites between tasks

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --project <KEY>
          Registered project ID instead of the current Git common-directory binding

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --owner <NAME>
          Actor for claims and events; defaults to the invoking agent's live runtime (`DOTS_AGENT_OWNER` when it names the invoking session), else its session (pi-$PI_SESSION_ID, claude-$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, or codex-$CODEX_SESSION_ID); supply explicitly for direct CLI use

      --fresh
          Run one sync pass first, importing other machines' current trees (when sharing is on)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots task goal coordinate

```text
Claim a goal's root as its coordinator. Only the coordinator dispatches, edits, accepts or closes the goal's tasks; other sessions read. Coordination is responsibility, not dispatch: it works with unfinished children, prerequisites and held work. A managed worker (DOTS_WORKER_ID set) cannot coordinate, and a Pi session needs its live runtime owner unless --owner is given. Another owner's claim on the root or any descendant fails unless --take, which moves every such claim to this owner in one transaction and records each transfer. A held (paused) or closed root needs --resume, which reopens it. Coordinating again is a no-op. Stop coordinating with dots task release ID; pause with dots task hold ID, which holds every descendant.

Usage: dots task goal coordinate [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>


Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --project <KEY>
          Registered project ID instead of the current Git common-directory binding

      --take
          Take over claims held by other owners on the root and its descendants

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --owner <NAME>
          Actor for claims and events; defaults to the invoking agent's live runtime (`DOTS_AGENT_OWNER` when it names the invoking session), else its session (pi-$PI_SESSION_ID, claude-$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, or codex-$CODEX_SESSION_ID); supply explicitly for direct CLI use

      --resume
          Reopen a held or closed goal root before coordinating it

      --fresh
          Run one sync pass first, importing other machines' current trees (when sharing is on)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

Claims below a root, held or closed roots, and released or taken-over roots are not coordination. A claim records responsibility, not that its session is running. Reads only the catalog; it never initializes one, and --project does not apply.

## dots task share

```text
Off by default and switched per machine. While on, every goal or top-level task tree of a project bound to a shared identity (dots project share) replicates on the substrate (dots substrate). One machine, the tree's home, changes a tree: its writes commit locally at once and the sync agent pushes them within the push budget. Other machines import the tree read-only on each sync pass (or --fresh) and refuse changes to it, naming dots task share take. Unbound projects and live claims never leave the machine.

Usage: dots task share [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  enable   Turn sharing on for this machine and queue every bound project's trees for export
  disable  Turn sharing off; imported trees stay read-only as last seen
  status   Show this machine's switch, trees, pending replication, withheld parts and updates refused after a takeover
  take     Make this machine the home of a tree imported from another machine

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --project <KEY>
          Registered project ID instead of the current Git common-directory binding

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --owner <NAME>
          Actor for claims and events; defaults to the invoking agent's live runtime (`DOTS_AGENT_OWNER` when it names the invoking session), else its session (pi-$PI_SESSION_ID, claude-$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, or codex-$CODEX_SESSION_ID); supply explicitly for direct CLI use

      --fresh
          Run one sync pass first, importing other machines' current trees (when sharing is on)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots task events

```text
Project history after an event seq, oldest first; use the last seen seq as a cursor. dots task event-kinds lists the kinds an event can have.
With --json the page also carries head, the project's newest seq (0 before its first event), even with --under; --limit 0 returns only the head, a starting cursor for reading what follows.
--under ID keeps only events on that task and its descendants, judged by the task tree at each read: tasks created in or moved into it count from then on, and a task moved out stops counting. An ID outside the project is an error.
--follow keeps running instead of returning a page: it prints every event after --since, then each new event as any session commits it, within about a second, one per line with no gaps or repeats. With --json each line is one event object, shaped like an item of the events array (NDJSON). It exits 0 when its output closes or on SIGTERM, SIGINT, or SIGHUP. A storage failure ends it nonzero with the error on stderr; with --json it also prints one {"error": ...} line. To resume after a restart, pass the seq of the last event received as --since.

Usage: dots task events [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --project <KEY>
          Registered project ID instead of the current Git common-directory binding

      --since <SINCE>
          Only events with seq greater than this (default 0)

          [default: 0]

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum events to return (0 for only the head); --follow streams every event instead

          [default: 100]

      --owner <NAME>
          Actor for claims and events; defaults to the invoking agent's live runtime (`DOTS_AGENT_OWNER` when it names the invoking session), else its session (pi-$PI_SESSION_ID, claude-$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, or codex-$CODEX_SESSION_ID); supply explicitly for direct CLI use

      --fresh
          Run one sync pass first, importing other machines' current trees (when sharing is on)

      --under <ID>
          Only events on this task and its descendants

      --follow
          Keep printing events as they commit, one per line, until stopped

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots task claim

```text
Claim a task for this session. Fails if the task is blocked, has unfinished children, is neither open nor in review, or is claimed by another session; --take takes over a claim whose session has stopped working on it. Claiming your own task again changes nothing. Review tasks need an explicit ID. --next claims the oldest ready task without children, optionally under --parent, and exits 1 when nothing is ready.

Usage: dots task claim [OPTIONS] [ID]

Arguments:
  [ID]
          Task ID; omit with --next

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --next
          Claim the oldest ready task instead of a specific ID

      --project <KEY>
          Registered project ID instead of the current Git common-directory binding

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --owner <NAME>
```

## dots memory

```text
Shared knowledge on the cross-machine substrate (see dots substrate). One snapshot pins all global/project documents and the shared project registry; its ID is the SHA-256 of its manifest. Reads never contact the remote: they serve this machine's local copy, which the sync agent (dots sync run) keeps current, and report its freshness: when it was last confirmed current (as_of, age_seconds), stale once that is over two minutes old, and the failing sync's error. --fresh runs one sync pass first. A machine that has never synced has no copy and says so. Publication syncs, then changes a batch against an expected snapshot: disjoint concurrent changes merge, same-document divergence waits for memory reconcile, and offline or repeatedly pre-empted publications stay pending on this machine. Tasks and outputs replicate only through dots task share; credentials and checkout bindings remain machine-local.

Usage: dots memory [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init       Publish the first, empty snapshot to the substrate; refuses if knowledge exists
  context    Read both MEMORY.md indexes at one snapshot from the local copy
  status     Show the current snapshot, freshness and retained candidates with their integration plans
  read       Read a published page; scope is global or an exact shared project ID
  write      Publish one UTF-8 page against an expected snapshot; empty content is not removal
  remove     Remove one page against an expected snapshot; retain its published history
  publish    Atomically publish a JSON array of changes against one expected snapshot
  search     Literal search at one published snapshot; default is global plus this bound project
  project    Manage shared identities and their separate machine-local catalog bindings
  reconcile  Publish a retained candidate against the head its plan names, with explicit choices
  inspect    Read a page of a retained, unpublished candidate, labeled as such

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --project <ID>
          Registered project ID instead of resolving the current checkout

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --fresh
          Run one sync pass before reading, instead of serving the local copy as is

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots memory publish

```text
Publish a JSON array from --input-file (use - for bounded stdin). For one page use memory write or memory remove. Each change has scope ({kind:global} or {kind:project,project:SHARED_ID}), path, and action ({kind:write,content:TEXT} or {kind:remove}); JSON keys and string values need quotes. All changes share --expected-snapshot from context/read. If knowledge moved on since that snapshot, changes to other documents merge automatically into a two-parent snapshot; a document that also changed elsewhere fails the publication and retains it as a candidate for memory reconcile. Offline, the publication is retained as a pending candidate (state pending) and published by the next online publication or reconcile. Empty files and removals are distinct.

Usage: dots memory publish [OPTIONS] --expected-snapshot <EXPECTED_SNAPSHOT> --input-file <INPUT_FILE>

Options:
      --expected-snapshot <EXPECTED_SNAPSHOT>


      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --project <ID>
          Registered project ID instead of resolving the current checkout

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --fresh
          Run one sync pass before reading, instead of serving the local copy as is

      --input-file <INPUT_FILE>
          JSON file, or - to read bounded changes from stdin

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots memory reconcile

```text
Read JSON {local, incoming, resolutions} from --input-file (use - for bounded stdin): local is a retained candidate and incoming the published snapshot from its plan in memory status. Each resolution names one conflicting resource and a choice: {kind:local}, {kind:incoming}, {kind:write,content:TEXT} or {kind:remove}. Every conflict needs exactly one choice; a candidate without conflicts takes an empty list. If knowledge moved past incoming, nothing changes; re-plan from memory status.

Usage: dots memory reconcile [OPTIONS] --input-file <INPUT_FILE>

Options:
      --input-file <INPUT_FILE>


      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --project <ID>
          Registered project ID instead of resolving the current checkout

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --fresh
          Run one sync pass before reading, instead of serving the local copy as is

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots substrate

```text
The substrate stores content-addressed blobs and compare-and-swap refs in one shared Git remote. Each machine keeps a verified blob cache, a Git cache repository and a SQLite state database (listing and freshness record, known values, outbox, stranded updates, push budget, sync health, counters and machine identity) under $XDG_DATA_HOME/dots/substrate (default ~/.local/share/dots/substrate). Domains such as memory read the local copy; dots sync keeps it current. This group configures the remote and reports local state.

Usage: dots substrate [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init    Point this machine at its shared remote; refuses to change an existing configuration
  status  Show the remote, machine identity, last pass and error, backoff, unflushed and stranded updates and counters without networking

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## dots substrate init

```text
Write this machine's substrate configuration: the Git remote URL (a private repository such as https://github.com/OWNER/REPO.git, or file:// for tests) and an optional Git credential helper command, such as '!gh auth git-credential'. Credentials come only from that helper; dots never reads or stores tokens. An identical rerun succeeds; changing an existing configuration is refused.

Usage: dots substrate init [OPTIONS] --remote <URL>

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --remote <URL>


      --credential-helper <CMD>


      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

```text
      --directory <PATH>

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## dots sync

```text
A sync pass lists every ref in one request (5 second deadline), fetches the values that changed into the local cache, flushes deferred updates within the push budget and records the outcome. Passes are idempotent and run one at a time per machine; a failed pass backs off later scheduled passes with jittered exponential delays (5 seconds doubling to 5 minutes). Without a configured substrate there is nothing to sync.

Usage: dots sync [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  once  Run one sync pass now, waiting for one in progress, then pack the Git cache if needed
  run   Run the per-machine sync agent until SIGTERM or SIGINT

Options:
      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --directory <PATH>
```

## dots sync run

```text
The sync agent the login service runs. It runs a scheduled pass every --interval seconds (sooner when another process ran the last one), immediately when a local writer touches the state directory's changes marker with updates to flush, and on watch hints, which lengthen the period up to --resync. Failed passes back off. After passes that moved data it packs the Git cache once loose objects pass a few thousand. Until the substrate is configured it idles. It exits 0 on SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP after the pass in progress, and nonzero when the state schema is newer than this binary (as after an upgrade) or the state cannot be read, so the service manager restarts the installed binary.

Usage: dots sync run [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --interval <SECONDS>
          [default: 20]

      --json
          Return JSON instead of readable output

      --directory <PATH>
          Working directory for commands that use checkout context

      --resync <SECONDS>
          [default: 600]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```
